topic:
The simultaneous-exposure frontier for global treatment effects on random regular networks. For every admissible integer sequence n→∞, 3≤d_n=o(sqrt(n)), nd_n even, draw G_n uniformly from labeled simple d_n-regular graphs and reveal it to the experimenter. Conditional on G=G_n, potential outcomes y_i(z) are arbitrary real functions of z restricted to the closed neighborhood N_G[i], obeying n^-1 sum_i y_i(1)^2≤1 and n^-1 sum_i y_i(0)^2≤1; other exposures are unrestricted. Choose any distribution D on {0,1}^n, then observe one draw Z and all y_i(Z). The target is τ=n^-1 sum_i[y_i(1)-y_i(0)]. Define R(G)=inf_(D,measurable estimator) sup_y E_D[(τhat-τ)^2]. Both D and estimator can depend on G; no endpoint means are known and no prior outcomes, repeat rounds, or model restrictions beyond ANI are supplied. Determine an closed-form deterministic rate r(n,d), not defined as the original minimax optimization, and construct design-estimator pairs such that, for every admissible degree sequence, with probability 1-o(1) over G_n, c r(n,d_n) ≤ R(G_n) ≤ C r(n,d_n), with universal positive constants. Deliver matching bounds including any essential logarithmic or transition factors, and a finite graph computation route producing the attaining design or certified approximation at the same rate. The answer r is open: do not assume d/n or d²/n. Inferential corollary: derive a computable nonvacuous design-based error/CI guarantee from the attained risk, retaining the full population GATE. The result must close the polynomial factor-d gap for diverging degrees; merely restating the original upper/lower interval is failure. FIELD CONTRACT: Resolve the full two-arm global-effect minimax order in the random-regular regime, with an attaining one-shot design-estimator and matching lower bound over every procedure. A one-arm HT bound, fixed-estimator variance optimum, worst-graph construction, logarithmic tweak alone, or repeated experiments is out of scope. PRIOR ART: Distinct from active exp_mixed_design_degree_frontier: its affine known-weight outcome model and mixed-estimator worst-graph d² construction do not solve unrestricted ANI random-regular risk. Distinct from banked exp_bipartite_minimax_design and queued AWRI finite-rule exact risk/spatial FPT/quadratic interference specification test. Full-GATE conflict graph lower/upper gap remains explicit in August2026 anchor; do not claim that the Jan2026 talk already solved it. CONSUMER: Shi et al. (2020), Freedom of choice adds value to public goods, PNAS117:17516–17521, doi10.1073/pnas.1921806117, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7395457/ . Their random-regular degree4 arm directly compares the policy in which everyone may freely allocate contributions with the policy in which everyone has fixed allocation; first-round participation and public-good provision are measured before feedback. They use two whole-network replicates per setup. The concrete consumer is sizing and randomizing this same all-free-versus-all-fixed provision comparison: whether a mixed assignment in a larger random-regular network can estimate the full-policy effect with a shrinking robust error, and how its precision depends on network degree. For a one-round local-pool outcome, only that pool’s members’ contribution decisions enter; all later-round strategic feedback, final wealth, and two-hop individual total payoff are outside this theorem. The theorem gives a robust ANI benchmark, not a claim that their exact behavioral model attains worst-case risk or that their finite networks were uniform graph draws. It may change the next experiment’s allocation between network size, degree and whole-network replication; it does not reinterpret their existing multi-round findings. This published policy comparison supplies the applied question, while the new design is the theorem’s prospective use.
PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The draft derives a finite-population Beta–Bernoulli lower bound using the maximum balanced pair of simultaneously exposed endpoint sets. A configuration-model argument for small degrees and a verified binomial-to-regular coupling for larger degrees support a lower rate d²/[n log(d+1)]. A single assignment generated by independent seed draws with replacement gives unbiased estimates of both endpoint means. The control covariance has an exact positive-semidefinite Schur-power expansion, producing a graph-computable risk certificate under the original endpoint L2 bounds. Conditioning seed multiplicities on the assignment removes hidden randomization metadata. Exact enumeration checks joint probabilities, signed and spiked outcomes, and this conditioning step. The full matched theorem remains unproved.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform high-probability bound ||B₂(I−11ᵀ/n)||=O(d^(7/4)) for the Boolean radius-two incidence matrix throughout 3≤d=o(√n), or directly establish the same-rate covariance certificate. Expand and independently audit the lower-bound constants and external graph-theorem applications.
EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact identities and test the Boolean matrix and actual certificate across all degree ranges, including near √n. A proved typical excess over the proposed rate kills this sampler spine; failure of the stronger O(d) conjecture alone does not.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/round1118_presolve_strongest.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The August 2026 minimax analysis proves only d/n <= R(G) <= d^2/n for the random-regular GATE problem. Its general conflict-graph procedure does not determine whether the typical frontier contains a logarithm, a degree transition, or another polynomial power. The prior CausalSmith affine mixed-estimator result concerns known weights and worst graphs and therefore cannot close the unrestricted-ANI, all-design, all-estimator problem. New work must combine a lower bound sensitive to balanced simultaneous revelation of both endpoint arms with an upper construction exploiting typical random-regular radius-two geometry rather than only worst-case conflict degree or spectral radius.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A deterministic closed-form r(n,d), universal c,C > 0, a graph-measurable one-shot design-estimator, and a proof that c r(n,d_n) <= R(G_n) <= C r(n,d_n) with probability 1-o(1) uniformly over every admissible degree sequence.

open_problems.why_unsolved: An assignment can reveal many endpoints from one arm while revealing almost none from the other, so an ordinary maximum independent set does not measure information about the treatment-control contrast. The required object is a signed closed-neighborhood packing: the largest treatment and control endpoint sets whose closed neighborhoods can be assigned opposite values simultaneously and whose sizes are balanced. Existing random-regular independence results solve a one-color exclusion problem, while the presolve Beta-Bernoulli argument remains unverified against arbitrary graph-dependent designs and estimators. The transfer from the configuration model to uniform simple graphs and all constants must also hold uniformly across the full degree range.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A high-probability characterization, including logarithmic and transition factors, of beta(G) = max_z min{|{i:N[i] is all one}|,|{i:N[i] is all zero}|}, followed by a fully quantified finite-population Bayes-to-minimax theorem yielding the corresponding lower bound against every design and measurable estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its conflict-graph formulation makes the endpoint-observability obstruction and insufficiency of the existing GATE lower bound explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Minimax information is governed by observable endpoint sets -> GATE conflicts are bipartite across arms -> one-sided independent sets need not reveal a contrast -> quantify balanced simultaneous exposure and turn it into a sharp converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace the maximum-independent-set statistic in its design-adaptive finite-population testing construction by a balanced two-arm reveal statistic and audit total-variation constants assignment by assignment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its converse already conditions on each assignment's observable exposure set; the missing step is a least-favorable prior sensitive to both signs of the GATE contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt configuration-model enumeration, switching, and transfer to the uniform simple regular model from ordinary independent sets to signed closed-neighborhood packings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems need exponentially accurate counts of forbidden local configurations; the first changed step is the first-moment enumeration because incompatibility now occurs only across opposite arms through radius-two overlap.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Sharp adjacency spectral estimates do not directly control B2 because Booleanization records whether at least one length-at-most-two walk exists, not the number of such walks; repeated paths, triangles, and codegrees introduce nonlinear collision corrections. Polynomial graph-matrix machinery addresses regular-graph dependence but does not directly cover this Boolean operator uniformly from constant degree to d approaching sqrt(n). The prior covariance-SDP and product-exposure arguments concern linear assignment moments or independent product exposures, whereas the seed design produces nonlinear, correlated treatment and control endpoint indicators with a Schur-power covariance expansion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a theorem proving ||B2(I-11^T/n)|| <= C d^(7/4) with probability 1-o(1) uniformly over all admissible degree sequences and deriving a graph-computable O(d^2/[n log(d+1)]) two-arm risk certificate, or a matching lower-bound counterexample identifying the failing degree regime and corrected covariance order.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination problem in which radius-two conflicts govern the full-GATE covariance and coarse graph control produces the polynomial minimax gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Endpoint exposures conflict through shared closed neighborhoods -> the proposed design induces a Boolean radius-two covariance operator -> coarse spectral control loses a degree factor -> prove the typical operator certificate or identify its failure regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Rewrite Boolean radius-two incidence as a collision-corrected sum of polynomial graph matrices, then adapt graph-shape decomposition, switching bounds, and high trace moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The covariance certificate is an operator norm of a structured nonlinear function of a uniform regular graph, precisely where iid matrix-concentration arguments fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Use local-law control of the nonconstant adjacency spectrum to bound the polynomial A and A^2 components after projecting away the all-ones direction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its degree range contains the target intermediate regime and supplies the sharp walk-count spectral scale; the remaining work is controlling Boolean collision corrections.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its regime-splicing architecture for spectral estimates on growing-degree random regular graphs, with separate sparse and intermediate-degree arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result must hold for every degree sequence from constant degree through o(sqrt(n)), making a uniform splice essential.

open_problems.why_unsolved: General unrestricted minimax risk is encoded by large exposure-conflict objects with independent-set-type computational barriers. Existing polynomial procedures certify upper surrogates or optimize within fixed cluster-design families, not R(G), while the banked exact compiler depends on a fixed-dimensional orbit reduction unavailable for a labeled random regular graph. The first proof step that changes is the finite representation: an algorithm must exploit typical random-regular structure to construct a realizable two-arm assignment law and estimator while certifying that relaxation and implementation losses remain within the newly established statistical rate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A polynomial-time randomized algorithm taking G as input and returning a samplable assignment distribution, measurable GATE estimator, and computable certificate U(G) such that its worst-case endpoint-L2 MSE is at most U(G) and, with probability 1-o(1), R(G) <= U(G) <= C R(G).

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames the divide between information-theoretic minimax risk, hard conflict-graph objects, and computationally efficient experiment construction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Minimax theory supplies a statistical benchmark -> the benchmark is encoded by hard conflict geometry -> generic algorithms certify only loose surrogates -> typical random-regular structure should yield a rate-attaining finite experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Use randomized priority conflict resolution and exactly computable endpoint-exposure probabilities as the algorithmic core, replacing global spectral scaling by a typical-graph two-arm allocation rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already converts an exposure conflict graph into a samplable assignment and estimator in polynomial time; the missing property is a certificate at the true minimax order.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its penalized min-cut formulation and semidefinite relaxation for worst-case GATE risk, adding simultaneous endpoint-exposure and certificate constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how a graph-dependent GATE design objective can become an implementable convex relaxation, although its current feasible class is narrower than all assignment distributions.

The finite-sample upper interval applies to bounded outcomes under known Bernoulli assignment

open_problems.why_unsolved: The endpoint-L2 class permits individual spikes and supplies neither bounded fourth moments nor the weak maximum-conflict-degree condition used by existing Wald limits. Cross-arm exposure incompatibility also leaves many covariance products unobservable. Prior finite-sample exposure intervals assume uniformly bounded outcomes and fixed Bernoulli probabilities, while completion-based variance envelopes concern fixed estimators and asymptotic normality. A verified worst-case risk certificate immediately permits graph-only Chebyshev inversion, but it remains unresolved whether a sharper data-adaptive interval or better confidence-level dependence is uniformly possible under only the L2 ellipsoid.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable interval C_alpha(G,Z,Yobs) satisfying inf_y P_D{tau in C_alpha} >= 1-alpha for every endpoint-L2 schedule, with radius O(sqrt(r(n,d)/alpha)) or better and a matching lower bound or optimality statement for its confidence-level dependence.

writing_exemplar.why: Its inference discussion separates point-risk control, conservative variance estimation, CLT requirements, and the observed high-degree GATE coverage difficulty.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A graph-aware design may estimate full GATE consistently -> interference makes its variance only partially observable -> standard Wald coverage needs moments and weak dependence absent here -> derive an honest certificate-based interval from attained minimax risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the characterization and convex optimization of estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds to the attained design's exact endpoint-exposure probability matrix and endpoint-L2 completion ellipsoid.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly handles arbitrary interference, complex designs, and zero joint inclusion probabilities, matching the target's variance-unobservability obstacle.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over conservative conflict-graph variance bounds and finite-sample Chebyshev inversion, replacing the generic spectral bound by the sharper attained-design certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the identical full-GATE exposure graph and documents why normal approximation can fail in high-degree regimes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exposure-specific inverse weighting and the design-based covariance decomposition while retaining explicit handling of exposure pairs having zero joint probability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target remains an exposure-mapping estimator but requires stronger finite-sample honesty than the foundational local-dependence asymptotics.

literature_map:
Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA) established finite-population causal estimands under interference, but partial-interference groups are much coarser than arbitrary graph neighborhoods.
Aronow and Samii (2017, AOAS; arXiv:1305.6156) formalized exposure mappings, inverse-probability estimation, design-based variance bounds, and local-dependence asymptotics.
Ugander et al. (2013, KDD; arXiv:1305.6979) introduced graph cluster randomization and exact network-exposure probabilities; favorable rates require restricted neighborhood growth.
Ugander and Yin (2023, Journal of Causal Inference; arXiv:2009.02297) randomized graph clustering to repair persistently poor exposure probabilities, but analyze a fixed HT procedure rather than all-procedure minimax risk.
Jagadeesan, Pillai, and Volfovsky (2020, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1705.08524) and Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi (2024, ICLR; arXiv:2312.04026) develop quasi-coloring and independent-set designs mainly for direct or spillover effects rather than unrestricted full-policy GATE.
Leung (2022, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:2111.04219) gives near-rate-optimal cluster designs and inference under spatially decaying interference, a different model from exact ANI on random regular graphs.
Viviano et al. (arXiv:2310.14983, revised 2026) optimize worst-case GATE MSE within cluster designs using min-cut and SDP machinery but do not optimize jointly over every design and estimator.
Kandiros et al. (arXiv:2411.10908, v3 January 2026) give conflict-graph randomization, a modified inverse-probability estimator, and conservative inference; this is an upper construction, not the random-regular minimax solution.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje (August 2026; arXiv:2608.04909) prove only the explicit random-regular full-GATE interval d/n to d^2/n for d=o(sqrt(n)), leaving the polynomial gap intact.
Their bipartite GATE conflict graph indicates that balanced simultaneous treatment/control exposure, rather than ordinary one-sided independence, is the relevant missing lower-bound statistic.
Cooper, Frieze, Reed, and Riordan (2002, CPC) characterize ordinary random-regular independence numbers, but not signed radius-two endpoint packing.
Bauerschmidt et al. (2020, GAFA; arXiv:1910.10121) and Sarid (2023, RSA; arXiv:2201.02015) sharply control nontrivial adjacency eigenvalues across growing-degree regimes; Boolean radius-two incidence is a nonlinear step beyond adjacency powers.
Xu (CCC 2025; arXiv:2411.14314) supplies switching-based polynomial graph-matrix norm bounds, suggesting a route to the covariance bottleneck while leaving Booleanization and the sparse-to-intermediate uniform splice untreated.
Harshaw, Middleton, and Savje (2026, JASA; arXiv:2112.01709) optimize estimable conservative variance bounds under interference, while conflict-graph Wald theory retains moment and high-degree limitations.
Shi et al. (2020, PNAS; doi:10.1073/pnas.1921806117) supply the applied policy comparison: free versus fixed public-good allocation on degree-4 random-regular networks, with first-round local-pool outcomes furnishing a prospective full-policy ANI use case.
